overview: This 315-page file traces Japan’s petroleum supply and wartime vulnerability through diplomatic correspondence, company reports, export-control discussions, and intelligence assessments. It covers oil trade and restrictions in China, purchases across the Americas and Netherlands East Indies, synthetic fuels, refining, reserves, tanker capacity, and payment controls from 1939 to 1944.
interest: Company records and intelligence estimates show how diplomats assessed Japan’s oil dependence and the effects of restricting supply.
